heading: Gratissimam Sane (Letter to Families) … The Year of the Family

items.text: Obey your parents, as Christ in Nazareth was obedient to Mary his mother and to Joseph the carpenter.
items.quote: obedient (Lk 2:51) as the 'Son of Man' to Mary his Mother, and to Joseph the carpenter

heading: I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 6 · "Male and female he created them"

items.text: Live as a community of persons united in love, after the pattern of the divine "We".
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 6 · "Male and female he created them"
items.quote: the family as a community of human life, as a community of persons united in love (communio personarum).

items.text: Be fruitful and multiply; fill the earth and subdue it.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 6 · "Male and female he created them"
items.quote: Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it (Gen 1:28).

heading: Gratissimam Sane (Letter to Families) · 4 · Prayer … Love and concern for all families

items.text: Let prayer be the heart of your home: pray together, for one another, and with one another.
items.quote: Prayer must become the dominant element of the Year of the Family in the Church: prayer by the family, prayer for the family, and prayer with the family.

items.text: Remain faithful to one another in the marriage covenant.
items.quote: remain faithful in the marriage covenant

items.text: Embrace families in difficulty or danger as brothers and sisters, with love and prayerful care.
items.quote: May this prayer also reach families in difficulty or danger... feel the loving and caring embrace of their brothers and sisters!

items.text: Live by God's moral order in the home so that your children will set out on the road of the good.
items.quote: living in accordance with the moral norm, so that the individual born and raised in it will be able to set out without hesitation on the road of the good

items.text: Let truth and love guide your relationship, not what is false or merely attractive.
items.quote: they contradict 'the truth and love' which should inspire and guide relationships between men and women

items.text: Pray for families throughout the world, through Christ, with him, and in him.
items.quote: Let us pray for families throughout the world. Let us pray, through Christ, with him and in him, to the Father

heading: I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 9 · The genealogy of the person

items.text: Welcome each child as a person willed by God for his own sake, including the sick and disabled.
items.quote: They must want the new human creature in the same way as the Creator wants him: 'for himself'.

items.text: Take responsibility for each child as one entrusted to your family by God.
items.quote: God hands man over to himself, entrusting him both to his family and to society as their responsibility.

heading: I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 11 · The sincere gift of self

items.text: Give yourself to your spouse sincerely, freely, lastingly and irrevocably, for the gift of the person must be lasting and irrevocable.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 11 · The sincere gift of self
items.quote: By its very nature the gift of the person must be lasting and irrevocable.

items.text: Promise and keep fidelity to your spouse for all the days of your life.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 11 · The sincere gift of self
items.quote: I... take you... as my wife (as my husband) and I promise to to be true to you... for all the days of my life

items.text: In conjugal love be ever ready to give and receive new life, so that your communion may become a communion of parents.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 11 · The sincere gift of self
items.quote: the common good of spouses is fulfilled in conjugal love, ever ready to give and receive new life

items.text: Receive each newborn child as a person and a gift, never as a burden or mere statistic.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 11 · The sincere gift of self
items.quote: The newborn child gives itself to its parents by the very fact of its coming into existence.

items.text: Care for the frail, helpless child who is totally dependent upon you and completely entrusted to you.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 11 · The sincere gift of self
items.quote: this frail and helpless being, totally dependent upon its parents and completely entrusted to them

heading: I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 10 · The common good of marriage and the family

items.text: Love, honor, and be faithful to your spouse all the days of your life; let your union be permanent until death.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 10 · The common good of marriage and the family
items.quote: I promise to be true to you in good times and in bad, in sickness and in health. I will love you and honour you all the days of my life

items.text: Make your conjugal union a union in prayer.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 10 · The common good of marriage and the family
items.quote: It must become a union in prayer

items.text: Accept the children God grants you and raise them as Christians.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 10 · The common good of marriage and the family
items.quote: the Church asks the spouses if they are prepared to accept the children God grants them and to raise the children as Christians.

items.text: Make prayer a regular daily habit in your family.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 10 · The common good of marriage and the family
items.quote: prayer needs to become a regular habit in the daily life of each family

items.text: Pray for all your family members.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 10 · The common good of marriage and the family
items.quote: Families should pray for all of their members, in view of the good which the family is for each individual

items.text: In family prayer remember and pray for deceased family members.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 10 · The common good of marriage and the family
items.quote: In prayer everyone should be present: the living and those who have died, and also those yet to come into the world.
items.conflict: Prayer for the dead is not taught in Scripture; it depends on purgatory and conflicts with Hebrews 9:27.

heading: I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 7 · The marital covenant

items.text: Give yourself wholly to your spouse and accept your spouse wholly.
items.quote: man and woman 'give themselves to each other and accept each other'

items.text: Leave your father and mother and cleave to your wife; become one flesh with her.
items.quote: a man leaves his father and his mother and cleaves to his wife, and they become one flesh

items.text: Let no one put asunder what God has joined together; preserve the indissoluble unity of your marriage.
items.quote: What therefore God has joined together, let not man put asunder

items.text: Hold your marriage indissoluble, for it is the basis of the common good of the family.
items.quote: the indissoluble character of marriage as the basis of the common good of the family

items.text: Receive fatherhood and motherhood as a task entrusted to you, and let them be a proof of love.
items.quote: Fatherhood and motherhood are themselves a particular proof of love... a task entrusted to both husband and wife

items.text: Consolidate your parents' covenant, enriching and deepening their conjugal communion.
items.quote: The children born to them... should consolidate that covenant, enriching and deepening the conjugal communion of the father and mother

items.text: Remain faithful to your spouse always, all the days of your life, and seek inner strength from God when love is tested.
items.quote: I promise to be faithful to you always... all the days of my life

items.text: Turn your hearts and thoughts together to God, so that your fatherhood and motherhood may be continually renewed in love.
items.quote: hearts and thoughts turned towards the God 'from whom every family is named'

heading: I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 8 · The unity of the two

items.text: Enter marriage by a mutual choice that is fully conscious and free, not by coercion or blind impulse.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 8 · The unity of the two
items.quote: a mutual choice which is, or ought to be, fully conscious and free.

items.text: Leave father and mother and cleave to your wife, becoming one flesh with her.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 8 · The unity of the two
items.quote: a man who leaves father and mother in order to cleave to his wife (cf. Gen 2:24).

items.text: Live your conjugal union in truth and love, as persons created in the image and likeness of God.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 8 · The unity of the two
items.quote: their union ought to take place 'in truth and love', and thus express the maturity proper to persons created in the image and likeness of God.

items.text: Accept children lovingly from God, and bring them up according to the law of Christ and his Church.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 8 · The unity of the two
items.quote: Will you accept children lovingly from God, and bring them up according to the law of Christ and his Church?

heading: II · THE BRIDEGROOM IS WITH YOU · 19 · The Great Mystery

items.text: Love your wife as yourself, as Christ loved the church and gave himself for her.
items.quote: Let each one of you love his wife as himself

items.text: Respect your husband because you love him and know that you are loved in return.
items.quote: let the wife see that she respects her husband

items.text: Make a free gift of yourself to your spouse, acknowledging his or her personal dignity and uniqueness.
items.quote: makes a free gift of self to the other and to the children received from the Lord

items.text: Obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right.
items.quote: Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right

items.text: Honor your father and mother, that it may be well with you and that you may live long on the earth.
items.quote: Honour your father and mother

items.text: Do not provoke your children to anger.
items.quote: Fathers, do not provoke your children to anger

items.text: Bring your children up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.
items.quote: bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord

heading: I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 13 · The two civilizations

items.text: Make a sincere gift of yourself to your spouse, and never reduce one another to mutual use.
items.quote: man cannot fully 'find himself' except through the sincere gift of self

items.text: Exercise responsible fatherhood and motherhood as part of the civilization of love.
items.quote: responsible fatherhood and motherhood is an integral part of the 'civilization of love'

items.text: Never treat your wife as an object for your use.
items.quote: woman can become an object for man

items.text: Never treat your children as a hindrance.
items.quote: children a hindrance to parents

heading: I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 14 · Love is demanding

items.text: Love one another with the love that is patient and kind and endures all things.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 14 · Love is demanding
items.quote: love which is 'patient' and 'kind', and 'endures all things' (1 Cor 13:4, 7)—is certainly a demanding love.

items.text: Remain faithful to your covenant with God, even when the road becomes difficult.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 14 · Love is demanding
items.quote: they will be faithful to their covenant with God.

items.text: Love your children with a healing love, and never deprive them of a father or mother.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 14 · Love is demanding
items.quote: the ones who end up paying are, apart from the other spouse, the children, deprived of a father or mother

items.text: Seek forgiveness and reconciliation by encountering Christ through the Sacrament of Penance.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 14 · Love is demanding
items.quote: family members need to encounter Christ in the Church through the wonderful Sacrament of Penance and Reconciliation.
items.conflict: Reformed Christians confess sins directly to God through Christ alone; sacramental penance is not a biblical requirement.

items.text: Pray for married couples to love their vocation and be faithful to their covenant with God, even on hard roads.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 14 · Love is demanding
items.quote: We need to pray that married couples will love their vocation, even when the road becomes difficult

heading: II · THE BRIDEGROOM IS WITH YOU · 19 · The Great Mystery

items.text: Love her as Christ loved the Church and gave himself up for her.
items.quote: Husbands, love your wives, as Christ loved the Church and gave himself up for her

items.text: Love her as your own body; nourish and cherish her as Christ does the Church.
items.quote: husbands should love their wives as their own bodies... nourishes and cherishes it, as Christ does the Church

items.text: Be subject to one another out of reverence for Christ.
items.quote: Be subject to one another out of reverence for Christ

items.text: Leave your father and mother and cleave to your wife, becoming one flesh.
items.quote: A man leaves his father and his mother and cleaves to his wife, and they become one flesh

items.text: Share in Christ's love so that you may love one another to the end.
items.quote: Only if husbands and wives share in that love and in that 'great mystery' can they love 'to the end'

heading: II · THE BRIDEGROOM IS WITH YOU · 21 · Birth and Danger

items.text: Guard your wife and children from danger, as Joseph took the child and his mother to Egypt to escape Herod.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, II · THE BRIDEGROOM IS WITH YOU · 21 · Birth and Danger
items.quote: the fatherly care of Joseph, who takes him with his mother into Egypt, where they remain until Herod's death.

items.text: Never kill the child in the womb, but protect its life from conception as a gift, not an object of use.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, II · THE BRIDEGROOM IS WITH YOU · 21 · Birth and Danger
items.quote: God commands: "You shall not kill" (Ex 20:13).

heading: I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 17 · Family and society

items.text: Honor the marriage covenant: establish a partnership of the whole of life and seek one another's well-being.
items.quote: a partnership of their whole life, and which of its own very nature is ordered to the well-being of the spouses and to the procreation and upbringing of children.

items.text: Procreate responsibly and educate your children.
items.quote: the right of parents to responsible procreation and the education of children

items.text: Nourish, care for, and devote yourself to your child's upbringing, especially in the early years.
items.quote: a woman who, having given birth to a child, nourishes and cares for that child and devotes herself to its upbringing, particularly in the early years

heading: II · THE BRIDEGROOM IS WITH YOU · 22 · "You welcomed me"

items.text: Be the first witnesses and servants of your children's rebirth in the Holy Spirit.
items.quote: You yourselves, dear fathers and mothers, are the first witnesses and servants of this rebirth in the Holy Spirit.

items.text: Welcome the unborn child and let him be born.
items.quote: I was an unborn child, and you welcomed me by letting me be born

items.text: Do not reject the child you have conceived.
items.quote: the child conceived and then rejected: 'You did not welcome me'!

items.text: Do not abandon your wife or husband; in her or him you welcome or reject Christ.
items.quote: he would identify with the abandoned wife or husband

items.text: Adopt the orphan and raise him as your own child.
items.quote: I was an orphan, and you adopted me and raised me as one of your own children.

items.text: Help mothers who are uncertain or under pressure to welcome and let their unborn child be born.
items.quote: You helped mothers filled with uncertainty and exposed to wrongful pressure to welcome their unborn child and let it be born

items.text: Help large families and families in difficulty to look after and educate the children God gave them.
items.quote: You helped large families and families in difficulty to look after and educate the children God gave them

items.text: Honor your father and mother as the Fourth Commandment requires.
items.quote: including those we have discussed in this Letter: the Fourth, Fifth, Sixth and Ninth Commandments

heading: I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 16 · Education

items.text: Honor your father and mother.
items.quote: Honour your father and your mother (Ex 20:12)

items.text: Honor your children, whether young or old, recognizing and respecting them as persons.
items.quote: Parents are also called to 'honour' their children, whether they are young or old.

items.text: Choose for your children a religious and moral education consonant with your convictions, and remain active in their education even when others teach them.
items.quote: families, and more specifically parents, are free to choose for their children a particular kind of religious and moral education consonant with their own convictions.

items.text: Prepare your children for their future vocation, especially for marriage.
items.quote: preparing for future life as a couple is above all the task of the family.

items.text: Build bonds of solidarity with other families, and assist one another in the educational enterprise.
items.quote: It is important that families attempt to build bonds of solidarity among themselves. This allows them to assist each other in the educational enterprise.

heading: I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 15 · The fourth commandment: "Honour your father and your mother"

items.text: Honor your father and your mother, for after God they are your first benefactors.
items.quote: Honour your father and your mother, that your days may be long in the land which the Lord your God gives to you

items.text: Honor your sons and daughters, for they deserve honor because they are alive and are who they are from the first moment of conception.
items.quote: Honour your sons and your daughters. They deserve this because they are alive, because they are who they are, and this is true from the first moment of their conception

items.text: Act in such a way that your life will merit the honor and love of your children.
items.quote: You parents, the divine precept seems to say, should act in such a way that your life will merit the honour (and the love) of your children!

items.text: Give and receive each other as spouses.
items.quote: the spouses give and receive each other

items.text: Welcome your children and educate them.
items.quote: declaring their willingness to welcome children and to educate them

items.text: Preserve the good of being together, for on it marriage and the family community are built.
items.quote: the family achieves the good of 'being together'. This is the good par excellence of marriage (hence its indissolubility)

items.text: Safeguard the family community by honoring one another.
items.quote: a community which must be safeguarded in a special way. And God cannot find a better safeguard than this: 'Honour'.

items.text: Be for one another and make room in the family to affirm each person as such.
items.quote: to be together as a family, to be for one another, to make room in a community for affirming each person as such

items.text: Do not hastily rid yourselves of aged, disabled, or sick family members; affirm and care for each person.
items.quote: when it hastily rids itself of people who are aged, disabled or sick

items.text: Pass on the imperative to be human, forming your children as sons and daughters of their country and citizens of the world.
items.quote: the family is in many ways the first school of how to be human. Be human! This is the imperative passed on in the family

heading: II · THE BRIDEGROOM IS WITH YOU · 23 · "Strengthened in the inner man"

items.text: Strive to unleash the forces of good whose source is Christ, so that the family may be strong with the strength of God.
items.quote: To the family is entrusted the task of striving, first and foremost, to unleash the forces of good, the source of which is found in Christ the Redeemer of man.

items.text: Grow in understanding of your family's mission in society and the Church by hearing the Word of God, by prayer, and by a fraternal sharing of life.
items.quote: grow in understanding of its particular mission in society and the Church by hearing the Word of God, by prayer and by a fraternal sharing of life.

heading: I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 16 · Education

items.text: Raise your children as a genuine apostolate, communicating truth and love.
items.quote: raising children can be considered a genuine apostolate

items.text: Be responsibly committed to providing attention and support throughout the pregnancy and, if possible, at the moment of birth.
items.quote: But he should be responsibly committed to providing attention and support throughout the pregnancy and, if possible, at the moment of birth.

items.text: Recognize that your wife's motherhood is a gift, and willingly take your own part as husband and father in her motherhood.
items.quote: the husband should recognize that the motherhood of his wife is a gift

items.text: Together communicate your own mature humanity to your newborn child as a reciprocal offering.
items.quote: Education then is before all else a reciprocal 'offering' on the part of both parents: together they communicate their own mature humanity to the newborn child

items.text: Accept children lovingly from God and bring them up according to the law of Christ and his Church.
items.quote: Will you accept children lovingly from God, and bring them up according to the law of Christ and his Church?

items.text: Be the first and most important educators of your own children, and let all other educators act only in your name, with your consent and authorization.
items.quote: Parents are the first and most important educators of their own children

heading: I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 12 · Responsible fatherhood and motherhood

items.text: Give yourselves to each other in love as a total mutual gift, so that your whole married life is a gift.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 12 · Responsible fatherhood and motherhood
items.quote: when the spouses, in giving themselves to each other in love, bring about that encounter which makes them 'one flesh'.

items.text: In the conjugal act, confirm in a responsible way the mutual gift of self you made in the marriage covenant, remaining open to procreation.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 12 · Responsible fatherhood and motherhood
items.quote: husband and wife are called to confirm in a responsible way the mutual gift of self which they have made to each other in the marriage covenant.

items.text: Do not artificially separate the unitive and procreative dimensions of the conjugal act.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 12 · Responsible fatherhood and motherhood
items.quote: The two dimensions of conjugal union, the unitive and the procreative, cannot be artificially separated without damaging the deepest truth of the conjugal act itself.

items.text: Never treat your spouse as a means of pleasure; respect the other as the end of every act.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 12 · Responsible fatherhood and motherhood
items.quote: The person can never be considered a means to an end... The person is and must be nothing other than the end of every act.

items.text: Acknowledge and accept the child conceived in your union; do not hide behind 'I didn't want it' or 'you are the one who wanted it.'
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 12 · Responsible fatherhood and motherhood
items.quote: The husband cannot fail to acknowledge and accept the result of a decision which has also been his own.

items.text: As father, take responsibility for the child from the beginning; do not leave the burden to the mother alone.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 12 · Responsible fatherhood and motherhood
items.quote: This is true especially for the man... How can the man fail to assume responsibility?

items.text: Assume together, before your own consciences and before others, the responsibility for the new life you have brought into existence.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, I · THE CIVILIZATION OF LOVE · 12 · Responsible fatherhood and motherhood
items.quote: The man and the woman must assume together, before themselves and before others, the responsibility for the new life which they have brought into existence.

heading: II · THE BRIDEGROOM IS WITH YOU · 20 · Mother of Fairest Love

items.text: Take your wife into your own house, and do not put her away even when the law seems to permit it; obey God's command for your marriage.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, II · THE BRIDEGROOM IS WITH YOU · 20 · Mother of Fairest Love
items.quote: do not fear to take Mary as your wife... take Mary and her Son into his own house

items.text: Take the son your wife bears into your own house and care for him as your own, even if you did not beget him.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, II · THE BRIDEGROOM IS WITH YOU · 20 · Mother of Fairest Love
items.quote: take Mary and her Son into his own house in Nazareth

items.text: Reveal yourselves to one another, become a mutual gift, and walk the path of life together as a new community in Christ.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, II · THE BRIDEGROOM IS WITH YOU · 20 · Mother of Fairest Love
items.quote: two persons called to become a mutual gift... We shall walk the path of life together

items.text: Ask the Holy Spirit to visit your hearts, so that your love may be a gift from God continually nourished in you.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, II · THE BRIDEGROOM IS WITH YOU · 20 · Mother of Fairest Love
items.quote: the Church in the Sacrament of Marriage asks the Holy Spirit to visit human hearts

heading: II · THE BRIDEGROOM IS WITH YOU · 18 · At Cana in Galilee

items.text: Leave your father and mother and cleave to your wife, and become one flesh with her.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, II · THE BRIDEGROOM IS WITH YOU · 18 · At Cana in Galilee
items.quote: a man leaves his father and his mother and cleaves to his wife, and they become one flesh

items.text: Do not put asunder the marriage God has joined; from the beginning it was not so.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, II · THE BRIDEGROOM IS WITH YOU · 18 · At Cana in Galilee
items.quote: What therefore God has joined together, let not man put asunder

items.text: Entrust yourselves to each other for your whole life.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, II · THE BRIDEGROOM IS WITH YOU · 18 · At Cana in Galilee
items.quote: the Bridegroom in the midst of the bride and groom as they entrusted themselves to each other for their whole life

items.text: Remember at what price you were bought: honor marriage as a true sacrament sealed by Christ's blood.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, II · THE BRIDEGROOM IS WITH YOU · 18 · At Cana in Galilee
items.quote: Spouses and families, remember at what price you have been 'bought'!

items.text: Educate your children—and yourselves—by the power of the Eucharist.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, II · THE BRIDEGROOM IS WITH YOU · 18 · At Cana in Galilee
items.quote: No other power and no other wisdom by which you, parents, can educate both your children and yourselves.
items.conflict: Reformed households look to Scripture and the Spirit, not the Eucharist as an independent educational power.

items.text: Meet for meals and live together in harmony, so that Christ is close to you.
items.citation: Gratissimam Sane, II · THE BRIDEGROOM IS WITH YOU · 18 · At Cana in Galilee
items.quote: When you meet for meals and are together in harmony, Christ is close to you.

heading: II · THE BRIDEGROOM IS WITH YOU · 20 · Mother of Fairest Love

items.text: Never cease to pray for the 'fairest love' that enables your mutual promise.
items.quote: Young people, spouses and families themselves should never cease to pray for this.

items.text: Be true to each other in good times and in bad, and love and honor each other all the days of your life.
items.quote: to be 'true in good times and in bad, and to love and honour each other all the days of their life'

items.text: Do not look at another person lustfully; keep your heart faithful to your spouse.
items.quote: every one who looks at a woman lustfully has already committed adultery with her in his heart

items.text: Do not treat your spouse as a possession, for he or she belongs to God.
items.quote: Through concupiscence man tends to treat as his own possession another human being, one who does not belong to him but to God.

items.text: Hear the word of God and keep it, so that the Holy Spirit may pour fairest love into your hearts.
items.quote: all married couples who are open to hearing the word of God and keeping it

items.text: Love your children, for the future and unity of the family depend on the mutual love of parents and children.
items.quote: the mutual love of husband and wife, of parents and children, a love embracing all generations

items.text: Love your parents, for the future and unity of the family depend on the mutual love of parents and children.
items.quote: the mutual love of husband and wife, of parents and children, a love embracing all generations

items.text: Visit Marian shrines and gaze upon the face of the Mother of God to find reflected the full beauty of God's love.
items.quote: visit Marian shrines and gaze upon the face of the Mother of God
items.conflict: Prayer and devotion belong to God alone; Christ is the one mediator (1 Tim 2:5).
